Scheduled feeding is a natural fit for VelaPaw, and the board has the hardware for it (the **PCF85063 RTC** on your board gives real wall-clock time). Here's how it'd work and the one real gotcha:

## The design

**1. Time source (the key challenge).** All the current code uses `mono_ms()` — *monotonic uptime*, not wall-clock. Scheduling at "08:00" needs real time from the RTC via `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`. So the prerequisite is: the RTC is read into system time at boot, and the user can *set the clock* (a fresh board powers up at epoch/1970). That's a small addition but it's the foundation.

**2. Schedule storage** — in the store layer: a small list of `{hour, minute, amount, pet_id (or "any")}` slots, e.g. Bob → 15g @ 08:00 and 18:00.

**3. UI** — a time-setter on the touchscreen: hour/minute roller or +/- steppers + amount, added either as a new **"Schedule"** tab or a section in **My Pets** per pet.

**4. Loop check** — in the main loop, once a minute compare current wall-clock time to each slot; if a slot is due and hasn't fired today, dispense (and log it, so Trends/My Pets totals include scheduled meals too).

## Which model — this is the product decision

| Model | Behaviour | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Timer feed** | Dispense at set times, no recognition | Simple, but can feed the wrong pet |
| **B. Recognition-gated schedule** | At a pet's meal time, feed it *only when it's recognized at the bowl* | On-brand (uses VelaPaw's multi-pet strength); no wasted/misfed food |
| **C. Hybrid** | Scheduled times + recognition feed as today; schedule is a "due" flag, missed meals catch up when the pet appears | Most robust |

For a *multi-pet* feeder I'd recommend **B (or C)** — it's what makes VelaPaw more than a dumb timer.

**"Clock now" is the feeder's current time of day** — what the device *thinks* the wall-clock time is right now.

It exists because of a hardware limitation we hit: **this board has no working real-time clock.** When we tried enabling the ESP32-S3's hardware RTC, it killed the USB console (three attempts), so we reverted it. Without an RTC, NuttX's software clock **starts at zero (1970-01-01 00:00) on every boot** — the board genuinely has no idea what time it is.

So:

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it is** | The current time the feeder is running on (seeded to `07:55` at startup so it's sane) |
| **Why you set it** | No RTC → the clock resets every power-on, so you tell it the real time once per session |
| **What it's for** | It's compared against each pet's **Meal time** — that's how the feeder knows a meal is due |

That comparison *is* the whole scheduling rule:

> feed if **`Clock now` ≥ pet's `Meal time`** *and* the pet hasn't eaten today *and* it's recognized at the bowl

**It's also your demo fast-forward.** Rather than waiting until 08:00 in real time, you just tap Clock **+5m** to jump the clock to the meal time and trigger the feed instantly — that's exactly what step 4 of the test did.

## Option 1 (recommended): use the board's *external* RTC chip — **PCF85063**

Your board has a **dedicated PCF85063 real-time-clock chip** on it (it's right there on the silkscreen you showed me: *"RTC PCF85063"*). It sits on **I²C** — the same bus already wired up for the touch controller, AXP2101 PMIC, and camera.

1. At boot, read the PCF85063's time registers over I²C (addr `0x51`, regs `0x04`–`0x0A`, BCD) → convert to epoch → `clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`.
2. When the user sets the clock in the UI, **write it back** to the chip.
3. It's battery/supercap-backed, so the time survives resets and power-off — the "Clock now" control becomes a *one-time* setup, not per-session.

Note I'd talk to it **directly over I²C**, *not* through NuttX's `CONFIG_RTC` framework — because enabling that framework is exactly what pulls in `RT_TIMER` and breaks the console. Direct I²C sidesteps the whole problem.

Then the internal RTC would likely coexist fine, and dropping the whole CDC stack frees the DRAM we overflowed.
